    3. Visualize (no download)¶

    With the viz extra (pip install "euroflood[viz]"), a FloodFrame renders straight from the index: no raster download. Static plots use matplotlib; interactive maps use folium. This tutorial tours the two main views (recurrence and footprints) and the options that make them presentation-ready.

    From here on we query with shape="bbox" (introduced in tutorial 02), a clean rectangular ROI, so the maps aren't clipped by Zutphen's jagged boundary that follows the IJssel.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    import euroflood as ef

cat = ef.floods("Zutphen, Netherlands", shape="bbox")
    import euroflood as ef cat = ef.floods("Zutphen, Netherlands", shape="bbox")

    Flood-recurrence heatmap¶

    A bare .plot() shows how often each ~90 m pixel flooded (darker = more recorded floods), derived from the index alone:

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    cat.plot()
    cat.plot()
    Out[2]:
    <Axes: title={'center': 'Flood recurrence (recorded floods per pixel)'}>

    It accepts matplotlib-style options, like a different colormap, a fixed vmax, and whether to draw the query outline:

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    cat.plot(cmap="viridis", vmax=5, boundary=False)
    cat.plot(cmap="viridis", vmax=5, boundary=False)
    Out[3]:
    <Axes: title={'center': 'Flood recurrence (recorded floods per pixel)'}>

    Pass event_id= to see a single event's footprint instead of the recurrence count:

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    one = int(cat.iloc[0]["event_id"])
cat.plot(event_id=one)
    one = int(cat.iloc[0]["event_id"]) cat.plot(event_id=one)
    Out[4]:
    <Axes: title={'center': 'Flood footprint: event 4049036842'}>

    Add a basemap under any static plot with basemap=True (needs network for the tiles): cat.plot(basemap=True, tiles="grayscale"). Presets are grayscale, dark, osm.

    Per-event footprints¶

    .footprints() returns a GeoDataFrame with one row per event, its extent_km2, and (when available) duration_days, useful as data:

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    foot = cat.footprints()
foot[["event_id", "date", "extent_km2", "duration_days"]].head()
    foot = cat.footprints() foot[["event_id", "date", "extent_km2", "duration_days"]].head()
    Out[5]:
    event_id date extent_km2 duration_days
    0 3732793625 2015-01-12 1.042 42
    1 1127339359 2015-03-09 0.492 42
    2 436160978 2015-12-28 8.025 56
    3 1434935811 2016-01-11 0.201 7
    4 2231395711 2016-02-08 4.939 42

    The same footprints as a static map, coloured by year:

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    cat.plot(footprints=True)
    cat.plot(footprints=True)
    Out[6]:
    <Axes: title={'center': 'Flood extents by event'}>

    Interactive maps¶

    .explore() returns a folium map. The default recurrence view carries hover tooltips (how many floods, when) and a click popup listing the dates. Pass tiles= for a different basemap ("grayscale", "dark", or "osm"):

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    cat.explore(tiles="grayscale")
    cat.explore(tiles="grayscale")
    Out[7]:
    Make this Notebook Trusted to load map: File -> Trust Notebook

    cat.explore(footprints=True, tiles="grayscale") instead puts each event on its own toggleable layer, foldered by year, the interactive twin of the static footprints above.
